specify.notes: Generated directly by orchestrator after two phase-executor attempts stalled without artifacts.

key_outcomes: release/cancel require active or explicitly cancellable stage evidence
retry can retire an active claim or target failed/stuck/stale/deferred/cancelled evidence
terminal task and terminal GitHub states are not retry-eligible
operator_released/operator_cancelled/operator_retry_requested release reasons defined
closed mutation outcome vocabulary defined
single mutation route is POST /api/tasks/[id]/claim-control
Idempotency-Key header is required and scoped to actor, route/action/task/stage target, and canonical parsed request body
same-key same-body replays return stable original successful responses while same-key different-body requests return idempotency_key_body_mismatch
activity rows alone are not sufficient durable response replay storage; Plan must add scoped idempotency storage or safely scoped shared storage
mutations use transactional compare-and-set predicates over visible task, workspace, stage, active claim or latest retry-eligible evidence, expected ids, cancellation state, and backoff requirements
closed HTTP mapping defined for success/replay, malformed input, auth, feature flag, not found, stale/conflict/not-eligible, semantic validation, rate limit, and sanitized unexpected failure
mutation authorization uses requireRole(request, 'operator') so operators and admins may mutate while viewers remain read-only
actor identity comes from authenticated request context and is never accepted from request body fields
mutation rate limiting runs before parsing or mutation and does not write claim-control task audit rows
successful mutations and authenticated task-visible semantic rejections write one bounded task-scoped claim-control activity
positive audit allowlist defined for action/outcome/state/backoff/actor/idempotency hash/correlation/error fields

raw idempotency keys, request bodies, errors, actor fields, prompts, transcripts, provider payloads, auth headers, GitHub bodies, tokens, and secret-shaped values are forbidden from audit/debug persistence
closed sanitized error category vocabulary defined
existing task_claim_reconciliation.v1 envelope remains the read surface and is extended backward-compatibly with optional claim_control fields
claim_control exposes authorization, available actions, retry eligibility, backoff, last operator action, last sanitized error, and expected-state predicates
available-action descriptors explain enabled/disabled retry/release/cancel states without exposing mutation URLs or raw diagnostics
SPEC-013D must echo expected-state predicates and refresh on stale/conflict rather than recomputing claim state client-side
extended read model remains side-effect-free and does not acquire/release claims, append attempt events, write activities, trigger GitHub sync, call scheduler/dispatch, or fetch live GitHub state
PR and UAT wording must state backend API/debug authority only; in-app adoption remains blocked on SPEC-013D and first real harness operation remains blocked on SPEC-013D plus SPEC-014B
target UAT uses a disposable workspace or product-line scope with FEATURE_TASK_CONTROL_PLANE enabled only through workspace feature flags

fixture set covers release, cancel, retry without active backoff, retry with active backoff respected, retry with override, same-key replay, body mismatch, stale/conflict, unauthorized/viewer rejection, feature-flag-off rejection, and read-model reflection
API/read-model/audit responses are primary evidence; manual database inspection is supporting evidence for row references and cleanup counts

evidence packet fields include replay identity, target deployment, commit, operator/timestamp, flag scope, identifiers, route/status/outcome, read-model before/after, audit references, idempotency hashes, backoff fields, override reason, sanitized error category, and redaction flags
cleanup uses unique spec013c-uat markers and records before/after residue counts for disposable workspace, project, task, claim, attempt, idempotency, and activity rows
rollback is flag-first and migration rollback evidence is required only if Plan adds a migration
UAT closeout records SPEC-013D as operator UX adoption blocker and SPEC-014C blocked until SPEC-013D plus SPEC-014B

key_decisions: add M79 release-reason constraint expansion and scoped claim-control idempotency replay table because activities cannot replay successful responses safely and operator reasons must remain claim-history truth
one narrow claim-control domain module owns retry/release/cancel semantics
existing task_claim_reconciliation.v1 read model is extended backward-compatibly

key_properties: dependency-ordered by setup, foundation, five user stories, and polish verification
TDD-first tasks precede every behavior-changing implementation task
M79 release-reason constraint expansion and idempotency storage are foundational blockers
SPEC-013D UI adoption and SPEC-014C harness adoption blockers remain documented
